title: SnowCal
description_html:
Implement SnowCal, a simple programming language used to perform calculations. A SnowCal program keeps a single integer X in memory, initially set to 0, and repeatedly performs addition and multiplication operations on it.

The language has 6 operations:

  • ADD Y — add Y to X
  • MUL Y — multiply X by Y
  • FUN F — begin the definition of a function with unique name F
  • END — end of current function
  • INV F — invoke function F (replay its body against the current X)

Examples

Input:  ['MUL 2', 'ADD 3']
Output: 3                          // X=0 → MUL 2 → 0 → ADD 3 → 3
Input:  [
  'FUN INCREMENT',
  'ADD 1',
  'END',
  'INV INCREMENT',                 // X=0 → +1 → 1
  'MUL 2',                         // → 2
  'ADD 3',                         // → 5
]
Output: 5
Input:  [
  'FUN INCREMENT',  'ADD 1',  'END',
  'FUN INCREMENT2', 'ADD 1',  'MUL 2', 'END',
  'MUL 2',                         // X=0 → 0
  'INV INCREMENT2',                // → ADD 1 → 1 → MUL 2 → 2
  'ADD 3',                         // → 5
  'INV INCREMENT',                 // → ADD 1 → 6
]
Output: 6

Constraints

  • Functions may be defined but never invoked.
  • Every invoked function is guaranteed to be defined.
  • No nested function definitions (a FUN body never contains another FUN).

Approach hint

  1. Parse pass: single linear scan. Maintain currentFn: string | null. On FUN F, set currentFn = F and start collecting into functions[F] = []. On END, clear currentFn. Otherwise, if currentFn is set, append the op to functions[currentFn]; else append to mainOps.
  2. Eval pass: walk mainOps with X = 0. For ADD Y: X += Y. For MUL Y: X *= Y. For INV F: recursively evaluate functions[F] (which itself can contain ADD/MUL/INV — no nested FUN so recursion is bounded by invocation depth, not parse depth).

Closest LC patterns: LC 736 (Parse Lisp Expression) — direct algorithmic analog (function table + recursive eval); siblings LC 224 / 227 (Basic Calculator I/II — state-machine evaluator), LC 150 (Evaluate Reverse Polish Notation — stack-machine foundation), LC 1106 (Parsing A Boolean Expression — recursive parse-and-eval).
